python - <<'PY'
p='/app/submission/planner.py'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('    def solve_dual(self, farkas=False):\n')
end=s.index('    def certificate_ok(self, y, q, farkas):\n',start)
new='''    def solve_dual(self, farkas=False):
        if farkas:
            # Split free q into q_plus-q_minus.  Besides keeping all internal
            # variables nonnegative, minimizing this L1 objective avoids huge
            # cancelling null-space components in a normalized witness.
            matrix = sparse.hstack((-self.A.T, self.E.T, -self.E.T), format="csc")
            normalization = sparse.hstack(
                (-sparse.csc_matrix(self.b.reshape(1, -1)),
                 sparse.csc_matrix(self.d.reshape(1, -1)),
                 -sparse.csc_matrix(self.d.reshape(1, -1))), format="csc"
            )
            objective = np.ones(self.R + 2 * self.K)
            rhs = np.zeros(self.N)
            bounds = [(0.0, DUAL_BOUND)] * (self.R + 2 * self.K)
        else:
            matrix, normalization, bounds = self.dual_data()
            objective = np.concatenate((self.b, -self.d))
            rhs = self.c.copy()
        attempts = (
            ("highs-ds", True),
            ("highs-ipm", True),
            ("highs-ds", False),
        )
        last = None
        for method, presolve in attempts:
            res = linprog(
                objective, A_ub=matrix, b_ub=rhs,
                A_eq=normalization if farkas else None,
                b_eq=np.ones(1) if farkas else None,
                bounds=bounds, method=method,
                options={
                    "presolve": presolve,
                    "primal_feasibility_tolerance": 1.0e-9,
                    "dual_feasibility_tolerance": 1.0e-9,
                    "ipm_optimality_tolerance": 1.0e-10,
                },
            )
            last = res
            if res.status == 0:
                zq = np.asarray(res.x, dtype=float)
                y = -zq[:self.R]
                if farkas:
                    q = zq[self.R:self.R + self.K] - zq[self.R + self.K:]
                else:
                    q = zq[self.R:]
                if self.certificate_ok(y, q, farkas):
                    return y, q
                # Another algorithm can choose a better-conditioned basis.
        if last is not None and last.status == 0:
            zq = np.asarray(last.x, dtype=float)
            y = -zq[:self.R]
            if farkas:
                q = zq[self.R:self.R + self.K] - zq[self.R + self.K:]
            else:
                q = zq[self.R:]
            return y, q
        raise RuntimeError("could not construct dual certificate")

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
